concept.title: What The October 29 Ruling Changed
concept.shortdesc: A federal court struck down the extra impairment test that CMS had added to the definition, and kept the limits on data and self-declaration.

conbody.p: CMS's June 2026 rule added an extra test on top of the five groups: the member's condition also had to significantly impair their ability to meet the 80-hour monthly requirement. On , Judge Richard Stearns of the federal court in Massachusetts struck down that added test. He ruled that CMS had exceeded its authority.

image.alt: June 3, 2026: CMS publishes the interim final rule. September 2026: CMS issues frailty guidance. October 29, 2026: a federal court strikes down the added impairment test. January 1, 2027: work requirements begin in most states. January 1, 2028: self-declaration narrows to once per enrollment period.

dlentry.dd: The court upheld two limits: states may verify frailty using only the past 12 months of claims and encounter data, and from 2028 members can self-declare only once per enrollment period.
The 25 states and D.C. that brought the case received a six-month pause on federal enforcement of frailty decisions, giving them time to update their systems.
CMS hasn't said whether it will appeal.

conbody.note: Build the impairment check as a setting your team can switch off, rather than logic written into every rule.
